result.explanation: For every encode event, recursively serialize the supplied JSON value canonically: object keys are lexically sorted, arrays retain order, and primitive spellings follow ECMAScript JSON.stringify. Return that string under key and preserve no meaningful state.
result.mapping: The event value maps to output.key through recursive canonical encoding; state is intentionally irrelevant.
result.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated JSON-value, depth, key, and numeric restrictions. JSON.stringify provides the specified scalar and string escaping behavior.
result.program: function solve(x){function c(v){if(v===null||typeof v!=='object')return JSON.stringify(v);if(Array.isArray(v)){var a=new Array(v.length);for(var i=0;i<v.length;i++)a[i]=c(v[i]);return '['+a.join(',')+']'}var k=Object.keys(v).sort(),a=new Array(k.length);for(var j=0;j<k.length;j++)a[j]=JSON.stringify(k[j])+':'+c(v[k[j]]);return '{'+a.join(',')+'}'}return {state:null,output:{key:c(x.event.value)}}}
